business_problem: AtlantiCare wanted to reduce clinician documentation burden and improve emergency department workflows without disrupting care delivery, so it needed a clinical documentation solution tightly integrated with emergency medicine processes and the EHR.
solution_summary: AtlantiCare worked with Oracle Health to redesign emergency department workflows around Oracle Health AI Agents, Oracle Health Emergency Medicine, ED LaunchPoint, and Oracle Health Foundation EHR. Oracle first performed a workflow and documentation assessment, then used a design-build-test-educate method to optimize physician processes and introduce AI note creation inside the emergency medicine environment. Voice- and workflow-driven documentation capabilities now draft notes directly within the EHR, while chart-review views help clinicians and nurses retrieve patient information more efficiently during ED care. Because the implementation was grounded in workflow analysis instead of a standalone transcription tool, AtlantiCare could align the AI documentation layer with emergency medicine processes, chart review, and team adoption across providers and nurses. The result is an AI-enabled ED workflow that shortens documentation time while improving usability and staff acceptance.

solution_components.name: Oracle Health AI Agents
solution_components.role: Creates AI-enabled documentation workflows that reduce per-patient note time for emergency physicians.

solution_components.name: Oracle Health Emergency Medicine
solution_components.role: Provides the emergency department workflow context that Oracle optimized before and during deployment.

solution_components.name: ED LaunchPoint
solution_components.role: Supports streamlined emergency department workflow transitions alongside the new documentation process.

solution_components.name: Oracle Health Foundation EHR
solution_components.role: Hosts the clinical documentation and chart-review workflows used by physicians and nurses.

data_flow: Patient encounters in the emergency department flow through Oracle Health Emergency Medicine and Oracle Health Foundation EHR, where Oracle Health AI Agents draft documentation and ED LaunchPoint supports workflow changes; chart-review views in the EHR then surface patient information for clinicians and nurses with less active time and manual navigation.
business_outcome: AtlantiCare reduced physician documentation time, lowered nursing EHR effort, and drove strong workflow adoption in the emergency department, improving both clinician efficiency and day-to-day quality of life for care teams and patients.
metrics: Physician documentation time per patient decreased 37%, from 5:36 to 3:18
99% of physician notes were created using the new documentation workflows
Nursing active EHR time per patient decreased 6%, from 7:53 to 7:36
Provider chart-review usage increased by 33 percentage points
Nursing chart-review usage increased by 40 percentage points
architecture_clues: AI documentation is embedded inside Oracle Health Foundation EHR workflows
Emergency department transformation included workflow assessment before implementation
evidence_quotes: Oracle Health worked with AtlantiCare to optimize physician workflows and documentation while implementing Oracle Health AI Agents and ED LaunchPoint.
Following implementation, physician documentation time per patient decreased by 37%, dropping from 5 minutes and 36 seconds to 3 minutes and 18 seconds.
By April 2026, 99% of physician notes were created using the new documentation workflows.
